correctness.rationale: For fixed-origin triangles T⊂B₂, radial vertex extension to the circle enlarges T strictly when any vertex is interior and preserves origin-inside condition. With circular gaps 2α_i (0<α_i<π/2, Σα=π), wedge integration gives I₄(α)=sin(2α)(2+cos 2α)/3. Setting θ_i=π−2α_i (Σθ=π), ∫ρ⁴=2/3(Σs_i−s1s2s3) for s_i=sinθ_i∈[0,1]; exact factorization 2−Σs_i+s1s2s3=(1−s1)(1−s2)+(1−s3)(1−s1s2)≥0 forces fourth radial moment≤4/3. Equality closure requires two θ_i=π/2, third zero: only right-isosceles triangle with diameter edge, disallowed because origin on edge; strict inf π−2/3 approached by admissible triangles. Differentiation independently verified I₄″(π/3)=0, I₄‴(π/3)=8, giving signed cubic −8t³ along (t,t,−2t); equilateral is a saddle. Finite barycentric moment checks verify normalization, not continuum optimality.
